selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only baseline provides useful signal and what performance floor should be used for later comparisons. config_001 tests the simplest RNA-only, single-profile, PCA representation without aggregation or fusion, isolating the baseline representation. It is the best first experiment under a limited budget because it is low-complexity, likely inexpensive, establishes a reference for RNA encoder and profile-setting effects, and avoids prematurely testing more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only baseline (config_001) with validation accuracy 0.4849 and F1 0.4639, so it is still unclear whether image features provide useful signal or whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing. config_010 tests a simple image-only ResNet50 singleprofile baseline, clarifying whether the image modality is competitive with the RNA baseline without introducing aggregation, fusion, or a more complex encoder. This is the best next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about a major design choice, modality, using the simplest informative comparison before investing in more complex multimodal configurations.

RNA-only PCA single-profile is much stronger than image-only ResNet single-profile in both accuracy and F1, making RNA the current promising direction while still leaving uncertainty about whether multiprofile aggregation can improve it. config_002 keeps the same PCA RNA encoder and model setting as the best completed experiment and changes only to multiprofile with simple avgpool, directly testing the profile/aggregation effect. It is the best next experiment under a limited budget because it exploits the strongest baseline with the simplest multiprofile variant, and it will either yield a stronger RNA baseline or clarify that profile aggregation is not helping before adding more complex encoders, image modalities, or fusion.

RNA-only PCA multiprofile with avgpool (config_002) is the strongest result so far, clearly outperforming RNA singleprofile PCA (config_001) and image-only ResNet (config_010). The main uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve on average pooling for the same promising RNA multiprofile representation. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder fixed, so it isolates the aggregation effect and directly extends the best current evidence. This is the best use of the next experiment because it exploits a strong direction while testing an important design choice before adding new encoders or multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and PCA substantially outperforms single-profile RNA and transformer aggregation, with both higher accuracy and F1. The main uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder such as scvi_n200 improves over PCA under this same promising profile/aggregation setting. config_005 tests this by changing only the RNA encoder while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, making it a clean one-factor comparison. It is the best next experiment because it exploits the current best RNA direction while reducing uncertainty about representation quality, rather than jumping to multimodal fusion where the image modality is currently weak and multiple factors would change at once.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models outperform image-only, multiprofile avgpool improves PCA over singleprofile, and scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool is currently best, but this is based on a single scvi experiment. config_004 tests scvi_n200 in singleprofile, directly comparable to config_001 for encoder effect and to config_005 for profile/aggregation effect. This clarifies whether the scvi gain comes from the learned representation, the multiprofile aggregation, or both, reducing uncertainty about a key design choice before spending budget on more complex multimodal fusion.

Current evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and scvi is the strongest setting (accuracy 0.650, F1 0.628), and multiprofile avgpool has also helped PCA-based RNA models. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the untested scGPT representation can improve on scvi under the same strong profile and aggregation setting. config_008 changes only the RNA encoder from scvi to scGPT while holding multiprofile and avgpool fixed, so it isolates the effect of representation. This is the best next experiment because it can either establish a new best RNA baseline or prune many scGPT-based configurations before spending budget on more complex multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool is the best configuration (accuracy 0.650, F1 0.628), and for pca_n2000 multiprofile, avgpool also outperformed transformer. This leaves uncertainty about whether transformer aggregation could improve the best RNA encoder. config_006 tests exactly that by changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and scvi_n200 fixed. This is the best next experiment because it is a clean, low-risk comparison that exploits the most promising direction and clarifies the aggregation choice before adding multimodal complexity.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile and transformer aggregation performs best (0.6530 accuracy, 0.6283 F1), with avgpool nearly as strong. Image-only resnet50 is weak, so it is unclear whether adding image features to the best RNA setting provides any benefit. config_032 tests this directly by adding resnet50 image features via simple concat fusion while keeping the same scvi_n200 multiprofile transformer setup as the best RNA-only baseline. This isolates the effect of multimodal fusion before spending budget on more complex choices such as ViT, weighted fusion, or other RNA encoders.
